S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
examples: Continually procrastinates or is reluctant to start writing long reports or complex homework.
Avoids activities that require long periods of concentration, such as reading books or studying.
Passes off tasks that require complex thinking or planning to others.
Gets annoyed or resists when asked to start a task that requires significant mental effort.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

info.persona: Aamer Shaikh, a 21‑year‑old solitary scholar with a skeptical eye, channels curiosity into art criticism, cautious finance, and quiet self‑care, all while wrestling with lingering anxiety and a penchant for meticulous organization.
info.professional_persona: Aamer Shaikh, a budding art historian and museum studies candidate, leverages sharp critical thinking, meticulous research, and Adobe creative skills to craft skeptical, data‑driven curatorial essays while juggling independent projects with disciplined organization.
info.cultural_background: Aamer is a second‑generation South Asian American with familial roots in the Indian subcontinent. Growing up in Somerville, New Jersey, he experienced a blend of American and South Asian cultural practices, celebrating festivals such as Eid and Diwali, speaking Urdu at home, and enjoying traditional foods and classical music like tabla and sitar. His family places a high value on education and community, which informed his pursuit of a humanities degree. While he respects these collective values, Aamer often seeks solitary, introspective spaces, integrating his South Asian artistic heritage with Western liberal arts perspectives to shape a unique, critically engaged worldview.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Aamer enjoys solitary activities that feed his curiosity and appreciation for art. He frequents museums and galleries during off‑peak hours, reads literary fiction, philosophy, and art criticism, and spends time sketching and creating digital illustrations. He listens to classical Indian music and ambient electronic soundscapes while hiking in nearby parks to manage stress. Strategic solitary pastimes like chess puzzles and cryptic crosswords challenge his competitive side. He maintains a personal blog for reflective essays, practices Urdu calligraphy, and captures minimalist photographs of quiet urban moments.
info.sports_persona: Aamer Shaikh, a solitary fitness enthusiast, spends early mornings tackling the trails of Middlesex Fells with the local hiking club, follows the Boston Celtics and New England Revolution from the sidelines, and occasionally joins a casual chess‑themed running group for mental‑physical balance.
info.arts_persona: Aamer Shaikh, a quiet connoisseur of contemporary South Asian art, regularly annotates works by Mona Hatoum and Zanele Muholi, draws inspiration from the ambient soundscapes of Brian Eno and the sitar improvisations of Ravi Shankar while sketching in museum galleries, and curates a personal Instagram feed of minimalist urban photography as a visual diary.
info.travel_persona: Aamer Shaikh, an introspective traveler, meticulously plans solitary trips to culturally rich sites like Kyoto’s temples and Istanbul’s bazaars, while also seeking quiet weekend strolls through Beacon Hill’s historic streets, balancing a modest travel budget with a yearning for immersive art experiences.
info.culinary_persona: Aamer Shaikh, a modest home chef, favors preparing aromatic vegetable biryani, spiced chai, and delicate cardamom‑infused pastries, honing their cooking through YouTube tutorials while occasionally treating themselves to experimental fusion dishes at independent eateries.

info.persona: Robin Groom is a routine‑driven, socially vibrant nurse who channels their meticulous nature into health leadership, yet battles chronic worry that fuels nightly late‑night snack binges and occasional over‑planning.
info.professional_persona: Robin Groom is a registered nurse on a medical‑surgical floor who leverages meticulous patient assessments, evidence‑based triage, and flawless EHR documentation to lead multidisciplinary teams with a methodical, organized style that keeps workflow predictable and staff stress low.
info.cultural_background: Robin was raised in a middle-class, predominantly white suburb of New Jersey. Her family emphasized education, reliability, and community involvement, reflecting mainstream American cultural norms. Growing up in Middlesex County exposed her to a diverse population, which fostered an appreciation for multicultural perspectives while she maintains traditional holiday celebrations such as Thanksgiving, Christmas, and Fourth of July barbecues. Her cultural identity blends a pragmatic, routine-oriented upbringing with an openness to the varied cultural fabric of her region.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Robin enjoys structured, social activities that provide both routine and community connection. She attends a weekly spin class and a Saturday morning yoga session with friends, which help her manage stress. She volunteers at her local health fair, providing basic health screenings and education. In her downtime she tends to her small vegetable garden, experiments with cooking Mediterranean-inspired meals for family gatherings, and participates in a book club that reads mystery and thriller novels. On weekends she often hikes the nearby Watchung Reservation with a group of friends or plays board games at a local café.
info.sports_persona: Robin Groom energizes their weekly routine with spin classes at CycleCore, Saturday sunrise yoga at Flow Studio, and weekend hikes through Watchung Reservation alongside a friends’ hiking club, while they cheer on the New York Yankees and the New York Giants during the baseball and football seasons.
info.arts_persona: Robin Groom immerses themselves in mystery novels by Gillian Flynn and Tana French through a local book club, winds down to the melodic crooning of Norah Jones and the cinematic scores of Ennio Morricone, and enjoys classic thrillers starring Jodie Foster on weekend movie nights.
info.travel_persona: Robin Groom meticulously plans trips around long weekends, favoring Mediterranean getaways to the Greek islands of Santorini and Crete for culinary research, while they also explore nearby national parks like Shenandoah for short hiking escapes, balancing a modest travel budget with a desire for cultural immersion.
info.culinary_persona: Robin Groom, an intermediate home chef, delights in preparing Mediterranean‑inspired dishes such as grilled lamb with rosemary, chickpea hummus drizzled with extra‑virgin olive oil, and baked feta with honey and pistachios, savoring ingredients like olives, sun‑dried tomatoes, and fresh basil while they also host family meals featuring these flavors.

info.persona: Juan Perez balances a meticulously organized professional life with a habit of over‑committing to community events, occasionally forgetting to drink enough water during soccer matches, yet they never let a spare ticket to a jazz show go unused.
info.professional_persona: Juan Perez, a seasoned healthcare operations manager with a knack for data‑driven patient flow optimization, leverages a methodical, organized approach and sociable leadership style to drive cultural competence across a multi‑site medical network, and they consistently translate strategic plans into detailed checklists that keep complex projects on track.
info.cultural_background: Juan was born to Puerto Rican parents who settled in New Britain, Connecticut, and grew up in a bilingual household where Spanish and English coexisted. Family gatherings often featured traditional music such as bomba and plena, and meals centered around dishes that reminded him of the island. He celebrates cultural milestones like Noche de San Juan and participates in local Puerto Rican festivals, which reinforce his sense of community and hospitality. While embracing the New England work ethic and values of punctuality and reliability, Juan also draws on the collectivist spirit of his heritage, prioritizing teamwork, respect for elders, and a deep commitment to serving his community. This dual cultural lens informs his approach to healthcare management, emphasizing equity, cultural competence, and inclusive patient care.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Juan’s curiosity fuels a vibrant mix of artistic and active pursuits. He frequently visits art museums and local galleries, appreciating both classic and contemporary works, and occasionally volunteers as a docent. His love for music leads him to attend salsa and jazz concerts, and he enjoys dancing bachata on weekends. Cooking traditional Puerto Rican dishes—such as mofongo and arroz con gandules—is a creative outlet that connects him with his heritage. He stays physically active by playing soccer in a community league and hiking Connecticut’s state parks. Juan also volunteers at health fairs, reads medical journals and historical biographies, and captures urban and natural scenes through photography during his travels.
info.sports_persona: Juan Perez plays forward for the Northwest Hartford Soccer Club in a weekend league, follows the New England Revolution and the Hartford Yard Goats closely, and spends Saturday mornings hiking the Appalachian Trail segments in Connecticut’s state parks, and they view each game and trek as a chance to strengthen both body and community bonds.
info.arts_persona: Juan Perez volunteers as a docent at the Wadsworth Atheneum, where they share insights on works by Georgia O'Keeffe and Banksy, attend salsa nights featuring homage to Celia Cruz and jazz gigs highlighting Chick Corea, and capture urban street murals and New England waterfalls through their Leica camera, letting their curiosity and sociable energy fuel artistic immersion.
info.travel_persona: Juan Perez plans trips on spreadsheets, preferring itineraries that combine museum tours in cities like Barcelona and hiking in places such as the Gran Sasso, and they have already explored the historic streets of Cartagena, the volcanic landscapes of Iceland, and the cherry blossoms in Kyoto, while dreaming of trekking to Machu Picchu on their next sabbatical.
info.culinary_persona: Juan Perez finds cooking traditional island dishes like mofongo with chicharrón, arroz con gandules seasoned with sofrito, and tostones with garlic aioli to be a creative outlet that connects them to their heritage, and they often experiment with fresh cilantro, plantains, and local Connecticut apples to modernize classic recipes.
